input.question: Why are indoor-only shopping malls dying in the USA?
input.ground_truth: Most indoor malls depend on the very large "anchor" stores to pull people in. These are your Macy's, Nordstrom, and other department stores, for the most part. These stores aren't doing nearly as well with the advent of online shopping, so the foot traffic to the other stores suffer. With less foot traffic, the smaller stores start to shutter, and it becomes a cycle. Strip malls are significantly less expensive and don't depend on their anchor stores in the same way.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why are indoor-only shopping malls dying in the USA?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big toy box at home where you can play with toys, but you can’t go outside to play in the park or with your friends. After a while, you might want to go outside and play with others, not just in your toy box.

Shopping malls are kind of like that toy box. A long time ago, people loved going to malls to shop and hang out because they didn’t have many other places to do that. But now, people can buy toys and clothes on their phones or computers at home, or go to stores that are outside, like big box stores or shops in neighborhoods.

Also, people like to be outside and walk around, or go to places like parks, restaurants, or big open shopping areas called “open-air malls.” These places are more fun and feel fresh because you can see the sky and breathe the air.

So, because people can shop online and like going to places that are outside and more fun, the old indoor-only malls are not as popular anymore. That’s why they are “dying.”
